basis: Intestinal hypoperistalsis, microcolon and megacystis define disease; hepatic failure in this syndrome is commonly related to parenteral nutrition.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; scoliosis 3/5 and hip dislocation 2/4 support skeletal involvement; astigmatism affects 2/4.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with seizures, intellectual disability and developmental regression.
Physiological withdrawal causes central nervous system dysfunction, including delirium and seizures; rhabdomyolysis is an occasional severe complication.
Congenital cerebral and cerebellar malformations with severe developmental impairment and intractable epilepsy.
Isolated developmental absence of the uterine body affects reproductive anatomy outside the axes.
Congenital globe, corneal and ocular coloboma abnormalities with myopia and impaired vision.
Premature hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal activation; accelerated skeletal maturation does not establish separate skeletal damage.
Neonatal epilepsy syndrome, despite generally favorable neurological outcome.
Hereditary neurogenic scapuloperoneal syndrome with muscle atrophy in 13/15 and intrinsic muscle pathology, including rimmed vacuoles in 6/8.
Infiltrative fibroblastic neoplasm of soft connective tissues; no additional organ is consistently affected across the umbrella.
Lip disease falls within the mouth and oral structures axis.
Hereditary skin/subcutaneous angioedema; normal-C1-inhibitor disease does not establish immunodeficiency; episodic mucosal swelling adds no lasting organ damage.
Neurodevelopmental and ocular abnormalities define disease; strabismus 4/5; pes valgus 3/5 and brachydactyly 2/5 support skeletal involvement. Otitis is separately coded.
ADD3-related cerebral palsy with spasticity and developmental impairment; dysphagia in 2/4 reflects neurological dysfunction without demonstrated digestive organ damage.
Muscular dystrophy with conduction disease and cataracts in 80-99%; cognitive impairment in 30-79%. Other manifestations omitted by cap; hypogonadism occurs in 5-29%.
Ataxia, immunodeficiency and cutaneous telangiectasia define disease; pubertal/gonadal dysfunction 80-99%. Muscle atrophy 30-79% omitted by cap; eye movements are neurological.
Defining malformations include thoracic/cervical skeletal defects, microtia and cleft lip/palate. Cardiac and ocular findings have unspecified frequencies.
Tuberculous infection of the epididymis; reproductive site has no organ axis, but the infectious mechanism applies.
IL21-related immunodeficiency with defining infantile inflammatory bowel disease; recurrent respiratory infections do not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
SARS coronavirus respiratory infection; kidney injury is rare, while headache and myalgia do not establish organ damage.
Androgenetic scalp hair follicle miniaturization; androgen responsiveness does not itself establish endocrine gland disease.
Localized benign neoplasm arising in the breast, an organ outside the axes; endothelial histology alone does not establish systemic cardiovascular disease.
Infiltrating carcinoma arising in bladder urothelium; lymphoepithelioma-like describes histology rather than lymphoma or nasopharyngeal origin.
Proximal tubular wasting with metabolic acidosis; phosphate-wasting rickets and leg bowing are major skeletal manifestations, although their frequency is unspecified.
